quick_notes.title: Tier 2 Focus
quick_notes.detail: More questions on Algebra, Geometry, and Cloze Test. Reasoning includes Critical thinking (Statement-Assumption).
quick_notes.explanation: In the second stage of the Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level exam, called Tier 2, you will see more questions on Algebra, which is the part of math that uses letters like x and y to stand for numbers, and Geometry, which is the study of shapes like triangles and circles. There will also be more questions on a Cloze Test, which is a reading passage with some words missing, and you have to pick the correct word from a list to fill each blank. The Reasoning section includes Critical Thinking, specifically a type called Statement-Assumption, where you read a short statement and then choose which unspoken idea or belief the speaker must be taking for granted for that statement to make sense.

quick_notes.title: Math Depth
quick_notes.detail: Check for 3D mensuration and Trigonometric identities.
quick_notes.explanation: Math Depth means the advanced topics in mathematics that you need to study for the SSC exam. 3D mensuration is the branch of math that deals with measuring three-dimensional shapes, like cubes, cylinders, and spheres, where you calculate their surface area and volume. Trigonometric identities are special equations, like sin squared theta plus cos squared theta equals 1, that are always true for any angle and help you simplify or solve problems involving sine, cosine, and tangent.

quick_notes.title: English Depth
quick_notes.detail: Longer RCs and complex Narration/Voice shifts.
quick_notes.explanation: In this topic, you will learn to handle longer Reading Comprehension (RC) passages, which are long paragraphs followed by questions about their meaning. You will also practice complex Narration, which means changing a speaker's exact words (direct speech) into reported words (indirect speech), and Voice shifts, which means changing a sentence from active voice (subject does the action) to passive voice (subject receives the action). For example, in Narration, if someone says "I am happy," you must learn to write it as "He said that he was happy." In Voice, you must learn to change "The boy kicked the ball" into "The ball was kicked by the boy." These skills require you to carefully track who is speaking and when the action happens, especially in longer sentences.

quick_notes.title: Reasoning Depth
quick_notes.detail: Focus on Syllogisms and Data sufficiency.
quick_notes.explanation: In reasoning, a syllogism is a logical argument made of two statements, called premises, from which a conclusion is drawn. For example, from the premises "all dogs are mammals" and "all mammals are warm-blooded," you can conclude "all dogs are warm-blooded." quick_notes.title: GK Focus
quick_notes.detail: Deep facts on Art/Culture and Economy (Recap).
quick_notes.explanation: This revision note is prepared for the Staff Selection Commission (SSC) examination. It covers General Knowledge (GK), focusing on detailed or "deep" facts related to Art and Culture, as well as Economy. Art and Culture includes topics like Indian classical dance forms, architecture, and paintings. Economy refers to subjects such as national income, budgeting, and economic policies. The word "Recap" means this note is a summary review meant to reinforce information you have already studied.
